chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Famous Door arrangements and how Kirby got his soft style
summary: Mosley's band plays elaborate arrangements; a manager makes Kirby play softly, and he reshapes his group.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You were on 52nd Street at that same time?
Oh yeah, I was at the Famous Door, and we were playing all these beautiful arrangements and even "Rhapsody in Blue", "Prelude in C Sharp Minor". I've got it in the book now.
You were doing most of these arrangements yourself?
Some of them, yes.
Who else arranged?

Lloyd Phillips (phonetic spelling) later made a lot of things for me. That's how John Kirby got his style. He would come over and listen to us, and when you look up and see other musicians, you're going to play your best, you play your best numbers and the manager came over with him one night and said, now look--because we played soft--the manager came over and he embarassed him right in front of me, now you're going to play soft like this or you're going to get the hell out of the Onyx Club--these were his words. Those were strong words and that's when John Kirby, he got this little short guy on trumpet--
Charlie Shavers?
Charles Chavers.
Charlie Shavers did most of the arranging for him.
Right. Then he got--
Billy Kyle.
Billy Kyle on piano.
He got rid of Pete (inaudible) and got Procope.
That's right.
And Buster Bailey.
He got the same--in other words, he had almost the same thing except he didn't have a trombone.
He had two reeds and one saxophone.
That's it, but I didn't need a saxophone because I played that, I played a tenor horn. He had a clarinet, saxophone and a trumpet but it was a three way thing like mine. When I played a clarinet--
I never knew you were on--I knew you were on 52nd Street, but I didn't think it was that early.
Oh, yes. John Kirby was next door at the Onyx Club at that time.
Oh, yeah, I was there.
